lessons.title: No Mockery, No Spying
lessons.objective: Name three harms of speech and suspicion
lessons.hook: How many ways can careless words and suspicion hurt a community?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: Let not any people ridicule another people

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: do not spy on one another or backbite.

lessons.summary: Surah al-Hujurat 49:11-12 warns against ridiculing others, and against spying and backbiting. Verse 12 also says to avoid much suspicion.

questions.prompt: Which of these does 49:11-12 tell you not to do?
options: Ridicule another people, spy, or backbite
questions.explanation: The verses name ridicule, spying and backbiting.

questions.prompt: Your group chat starts mocking a classmate. What does 49:11 point you to?
options: Do not join in the ridicule
Join in, it is only a joke
questions.explanation: The verse says not to let any people ridicule another people.

lessons.title: Kind Words
lessons.hook: What would change in your last argument if you had chosen kind words?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)

lessons.summary: In Surah al-Baqarah 2:83, among the things Allah took a pledge about is to speak kindly to people.

questions.prompt: What does 2:83 list among the commitments?
questions.explanation: The verse says: speak kindly to people.

questions.prompt: A disagreement is heating up. Which choice matches the verse?
questions.explanation: The clause asks for kind speech.

lessons.title: Swallowing Anger
lessons.hook: What does it take to hold back when you feel wronged?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: suppress their anger, and excuse [the faults of] the people

lessons.summary: Surah Al 'Imran 3:134 describes those who suppress their anger and excuse the faults of the people, and says Allah loves the virtuous.

questions.explanation: The verse describes those who suppress their anger.

questions.prompt: Someone makes a mistake that bothers you. Which response matches the verse?
options: Excuse their fault and let it go
questions.explanation: The verse says to excuse the faults of the people.

lessons.title: Patience and Prayer
lessons.objective: Use patience as strength, not passivity
lessons.hook: How do you keep going when things are hard?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: Take recourse in patience and prayer; indeed Allah is with the patient.

lessons.summary: Surah al-Baqarah 2:153 tells those who have faith to take recourse in patience and prayer, and says Allah is with the patient.

questions.prompt: What does 2:153 say to take recourse in?
questions.explanation: The verse says: Take recourse in patience and prayer.

questions.prompt: Who is Allah with, according to the verse?
questions.explanation: Indeed Allah is with the patient.

lessons.title: Honouring Parents
lessons.objective: Show respect and gentleness to parents
lessons.hook: What would gentleness toward your parents look like today?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: do not say to them, ‘Fie!’ And do not chide them, but speak to them noble words.

lessons.summary: Surah al-Isra 17:23-24 enjoins kindness to parents: not saying "Fie!" to them, not chiding them, speaking noble words, and lowering the wing of humility to them out of mercy.

questions.prompt: What does 17:23-24 say to speak to parents?
questions.explanation: The verse says to speak to them noble words.

questions.prompt: A parent repeats the same story for the third time. Which response fits the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse forbids saying 'Fie!' and chiding.

candidates: SAHIFA Supplication 24 (for parents, candidate): add when the page can be read.

lessons.title: Neighbours and Friends
lessons.objective: Widen kindness to neighbours and companions
lessons.hook: Who lives closest to you, and how well do you know them?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: be good to parents, the relatives, the orphans, the needy, the near neighbour and the distant neighbour, the companion at your side

lessons.summary: Surah an-Nisa 4:36 calls for goodness toward parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near and the distant neighbour, and the companion at one's side.

options: The near neighbour and the distant neighbour
questions.explanation: The verse names both the near and the distant neighbour.

questions.prompt: Who else does the verse list for goodness?
questions.explanation: The verse lists relatives, orphans and the needy.

lessons.title: Fair Even Against Yourself
lessons.objective: Stand for justice when it costs you
lessons.hook: When was it last hard to tell the truth because it counted against you?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: Be maintainers of justice and witnesses for the sake of Allah, even if it should be against yourselves or [your] parents and near relatives

lessons.summary: Surah an-Nisa 4:135 asks those who have faith to be maintainers of justice and witnesses for the sake of Allah, even when it goes against themselves, their parents or near relatives.

questions.prompt: Even against whom does 4:135 say to uphold justice?
questions.explanation: The verse names yourselves, parents and near relatives.

questions.prompt: Your friend did wrong and you are asked to testify. Which choice fits the verse?
options: Testify truthfully for the sake of Allah
Shade the story to protect them
questions.explanation: The verse asks for witnesses for the sake of Allah, even against near relatives.

lessons.title: Fair to Those You Dislike
lessons.objective: Keep justice when you dislike someone
lessons.hook: Can you be fair to someone you do not like?

sources.author: The Qur'an
sources.translator: Ali Quli Qara'i (Qara'i translation, via Tanzil)
sources.quote: ill feeling for a people should never lead you to be unfair. Be fair; that is nearer to Godwariness

lessons.summary: Surah al-Ma'idah 5:8 says that ill feeling for a people should never lead to unfairness, and that being fair is nearer to Godwariness.

questions.prompt: What should ill feeling for a people never lead you to, in 5:8?
questions.explanation: The verse says ill feeling should never lead you to be unfair.

questions.prompt: You dislike a coworker but must judge their work. Which response fits the verse?
options: Ask someone else to do it
questions.explanation: Be fair; that is nearer to Godwariness.
